cases.title: Publishing enforces the whole dependency closure, not the manifest
A complete lock publishes and the receipt records every package
Two signatures from one post do not satisfy dual control
One person cannot hold both approval posts
Two distinct posts approve and the release proceeds
Critical findings block regardless of approvals
A staging waiver does not authorise production
Publishing exactly at the repair deadline counts as expired
Waiver evidence pinned to another dependency version is refused
Extending the repair deadline retires earlier approvals
Raising severity retires approvals signed at the lower level
A transferred reviewer's approval stops counting
A risk on a transitive package appearing after precheck forces a new decision
Revoking one signature forces a fresh approval before publishing
Rolling content back to a retired digest is refused and flagged
One dependency reached via a diamond from two apps resolves once per release
A package allowed only in staging blocks the production release
Two paths demanding incompatible versions of one package is refused
Bumping the dependency or landing a verified fix clears the finding
A risk from another tenant can never authorise this release
Two processes approving and revoking concurrently settle on one consistent state
Two processes racing to publish leave exactly one pointer and one receipt
Publish commits before the escalation and the extension: it stands
A precheck token is spent once and a replayed request returns the same receipt
History keeps the receipt; the live query reports authority withdrawn
Superseded receipts stay readable and the pointer moves once
Invalid references and operations return their documented codes
A duty epoch bump after signing retires the approval
Only a valid simulated signature authorises a waiver
One reviewer signing under two posts is rejected
